qs.q: Gyro rigidity increases with?
o: Increasing RPM, and concentrating mass close to the center.
Increasing RPM and concentrating mass at the periphery.

qs.q: At what approximate date is the earth closest to the sun (perihelion)?

qs.q: The initial great circle track from A (S 27° 30' E 017° 45') to B (S 27° 30' E 029° 15') is:
qs.ex: Convergency = Δlong × sin lat = 11.5° × sin 27.5° ≈ 5.3°; half of it is 2.65°. In the southern hemisphere the great circle bulges towards the South Pole, so the initial track is 090° + 2.65° = 092.65°.

qs.q: Consider the following statements on sunrise and sunset.
o: in May sunrise occurs later at 4500N than at 4500S.
in November sunset occurs earlier at 4500S than at 4500N.
at equator sunrise and sunset occur at quite regular times throughout the year.

qs.q: When approaching the international date line from the east, you:
o: should increase your date by an extra date at the first midnight you experience.
should be prepared to decrease your date by 1.
should be prepared to increase your date by 1.
qs.ex: Book key prints (b). Approaching the date line from the east means you are flying westwards, and crossing it westbound you add a day, so the correct answer is (c).

qs.ex: PONTA is due north of PBN on the same meridian, so the true bearing from PBN is 000°. Apply the variation at the station (28° W): radial = 000 + 28 = 028°.

qs.q: Distance 'Q' to 'R' 1960 NM, Groundspeed 'out' 380 kt, Groundspeed 'back' 470 kt, Safe endurance 7 HR. The distance from 'Q' to the Point of Safe Return (PSR) between 'Q'and 'R' is?
qs.ex: PSR distance = E × O × H / (O + H) = 7 × 380 × 470 / 850 ≈ 1471 NM.

qs.ex: With the RMI card stuck at 075°, the needle reading 270° gives relative bearing = 270 − 075 = 195°.

True course from A to B = 090°, TAS 460 kts, W/V = 360/100 kt, Average variation = 10°E, Deviation = -2°. Calculate the compass heading and GS?
qs.ex: Wind is 90° to the track from the left: drift = asin(100/460) ≈ 12.6° → TH ≈ 077°, MH = 077 − 10 = 067°, CH = 067 + 2 = 069°. GS = √(460² − 100²) ≈ 449 kt.

qs.q: What is the true altitude of an aircraft if its altimeter indicated 16000 ft when the ambient temperature was -30° C?
qs.ex: ISA at 16 000 ft is −17 °C, so the air is 13° colder. About 4 % per 10° → true altitude ≈ 16 000 × (1 − 0.052) ≈ 15 200 ft.

Two points A and B are 1000 NM apart. TAS= 490 kt. On the flight between A and B the equivalent headwind is -20 kt. On the return leg between B and A, the equivalent headwind is +40 kt. What distance from A, along the route A to B, is the point of Equal Time (PET)?
qs.ex: In this question a negative 'equivalent headwind' is a headwind: GS out = 470 kt, GS back = 530 kt. PET from A = D × H / (O + H) = 1000 × 530 / 1000 = 530 NM.

qs.q: An aircraft was over 'A' at 1600 hours flying direct to 'B'. Distance 'A' to 'B' 3000 NM, True airspeed 390 kt, Mean wind component 'out' +55 kt, Mean wind component 'back' -75 kt, Safe endurance 9 HR 30 MIN. The distance from 'A' to the Point of Safe Return (PSR) 'A' is?
TAS = 197 Kt, True course = 240°, W/V = 180/30 kt. Descent is initiated at FL 220 and completed at FL 40. Distance to be covered during descent is 39 NM. What is the approximate rate of descent?
qs.ex: Headwind component ≈ 30 × cos 60° = 15 kt → GS ≈ 182 kt. 39 NM takes ≈ 12.9 min; 18 000 ft / 12.9 min ≈ 1400 ft/min.

qs.q: An aircraft is on an ILS 3 degree glide slope, which passes over the runway threshold at a height of 50 feet. The DME range is 18 nm from the threshold. What is the height above the runway threshold elevation? (Use the 1 in 60 rule and the approximation 6080 feet = 1 nautical mile)
qs.ex: 1 in 60 rule: 3° ≈ 3/60 = 0.05. 18 × 6080 × 0.05 = 5472 ft, plus the 50 ft threshold crossing height = 5522 ft.

qs.q: When the center of gravity is at the forward limit, an aero plane will be :
o: extremely unstable and require small elevator control to change pitch.
extremely stable and will require excessive elevator control to change pitch.
extremely stable and require small elevator control to change pitch.
qs.ex: Book key prints (a). With the CG at the forward limit the aeroplane is very stable and needs large elevator inputs to change pitch, so the correct answer is (b).

qs.q: By adding to the basic empty mass the following fixed necessary equipment for a specific flight (catering, safety and rescue equipment, fly away kit, crew), we get:

A jet transport has the following structural limits: Maximum Ramp Mass 63 060 kg, Maximum Take-Off Mass 62 800 kg, Maximum Landing Mass 54 900 kg, Maximum Zero Fuel Mass 51 300 kg. Fuel: taxi 400 kg, trip 8400 kg, contingency & final reserve 1800 kg, alternate 1100 kg. If the Dry Operating Mass is 34 930 kg, determine the maximum traffic load that can be carried if departure and landing airfields are not performance limited.
qs.ex: Limiting TOM is the lowest of: MTOM 62 800; MRM − taxi 62 660; MLM + trip 63 300; MZFM + take-off fuel (8400 + 1800 + 1100 = 11 300) = 62 600. Traffic load = 62 600 − 11 300 − 34 930 = 16 370 kg.

qs.q: Determine the Zero Fuel Mass for the following single engine aeroplane. Standard Empty Mass 1764 lbs, Optional Equipment 35 lbs, Pilot + front seat passenger 300 lbs, Cargo 350 lbs, Ramp Fuel = Block Fuel 60 gal, Trip Fuel 35 gal, fuel density 6 lbs/gal.
qs.ex: ZFM = 1764 + 35 + 300 + 350 = 2449 lbs (fuel is not part of zero fuel mass).

qs.q: Maximum Structural Landing Mass 125 000 kg, Maximum Zero Fuel Mass 108 500 kg, Maximum Structural Take-off Mass 155 000 kg, Dry Operating Mass 82 000 kg. Scheduled trip fuel is 17 000 kg and the reserve fuel is 5000 kg. Assuming performance limitations are not restricting, the maximum permitted take-off mass and maximum traffic load are respectively:
qs.ex: TOM limits: MZFM + fuel = 108 500 + 22 000 = 130 500; MLM + trip = 142 000; MTOM 155 000 → 130 500 kg. Traffic load = MZFM − DOM = 26 500 kg.

qs.q: An airway 10 NM wide is to be defined by two VORs each having a resultant bearing accuracy of plus or minus 3.5°. In order to ensure accurate track guidance within the airway limits the maximum distance apart for the transmitter is approximately:
qs.ex: Each VOR may be 3.5° off: half-width 5 NM / tan 3.5° ≈ 82 NM from each station, so about 165 NM apart.
